item.title: Can someone explain the entirety of the Scarlet King lore?: Re: Can someone explain the entirety of the Scarlet King lore?
item.content:encoded:
HAHAHA no that was a happy coincidence.

There's not really any definitive information about the Scarlet King as far as I'm aware. Djorc's Dust and Blood is the closest thing we've got to an official mythology (you may have noticed that it's crosslinked by 231 and KTE-2013-Kappala-Mendes), but it still has some contradictions to other bits, especially if you consider 2317 to be Big Red. I think Kappala-Mendes is the only document with any information about the actual cult.

So, basically, if you want to write something about the Scarlet King, just do it! Really all you gotta have is the number 7, maybe some faux-Satanism sex cult business, and some ancient Middle Eastern magic. Or you could have none of that, since there is no canon after all, and Tufto's proposal implies that the idea of "Scarlet King" could really be a whole assortment of different beings and organizations. Pick out what you like from what's been written, ignore what you don't, and fill in the gaps yourself.

item.title: Can someone explain the entirety of the Scarlet King lore?: Re: Can someone explain the entirety of the Scarlet King lore?
item.content:encoded:
Check the scarlet-king tag. Note, however, that the lack of canon applies much more to Big Red than to standardized, fleshed-out things like Sarkicism and the CotBG, so you’re going to run into some contradictions.

One of the most compelling elements of the Scarlet King mythos is the mystery. Unlike most other anomalous religions, most of the cultists are wiped out and the Foundation is left trying to piece things together from the artifacts they left behind. Toss in the subterfuge going on with 2317 and 231’s implications that the Foundation’s been infiltrated or something, and you have a situation where the people in-universe are probably just as confused about it as the reader.

item.title: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded:
Nothing. If this dude can neutralize 106 or some other impossible to destroy, nearly impossible to contain anomaly he could also flatten site 19 or eradicate the O5 council from existence, or make himself the supreme God emperor of earth or something. Reality benders are too powerful and too unpredictable for a control-freak organization like the Foundation to tolerate, no matter how cooperative they are, because they might become uncooperative in the future. That’s why most of the free-willed reality benders with full control of their powers in the SCP verse have either been decommissioned by Clef or liquidated by the GOC. If your character destroyed 106, the foundation would send Dr. Clef to kill him or otherwise make sure he doesn’t get the chance to destroy anything else.

Also, don’t make a superhero character and beat up 682. That’s a Mary Sue and the Worf Effect. Anomalous people, regardless of how helpful they ostensibly are, are monsters at worse and the victims of a terrible condition at best. If it has powers that you would like to have, it’s not an SCP. As a general rule, anyway.

item.title: apollyon class scps: Re: apollyon class scps
item.content:encoded: It's hard to paint all Apollyon articles with the same brush since they tend to go in radically different directions with their stories. Personally, I find the class more interesting because of the challenge that it provides to the author — you know, you're kind of expected to write to justify the usage of Apollyon, in a certain sense, which is an extra hurdle you put in front of yourself with the hopes it pays off.
